title: Cumulative Review 5: Modules 1 to 15
intro: Spaced review mixes questions from earlier modules. Retrieving older material now is what makes it stick. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: What is F, and is it significant at alpha = .05?
o: F = 6.33 with df (2, 27). It exceeds the critical value of 3.35, so yes
F = 6.33, but it is not significant
items.why: F = 63.33/10 = 6.33. The critical F(2, 27) at .05 is 3.354. The exact p is about .006.

items.q: The Spearman correlation is used when
o: The data are ranks or the relationship is monotonic but not linear
items.why: It applies Pearson's formula to ranks.

items.q: Multiple regression uses
o: Two or more predictors to predict one outcome
items.why: Each coefficient reflects the unique contribution of that predictor with the others held constant.

items.q: A researcher reports r = .85 for 30 points, but one point is far from the rest. What should be done first?
o: Examine the scatterplot and check how r changes with the outlier removed
Remove the point without saying so
items.why: Report both analyses and justify any exclusion. One point should not decide the conclusion.

items.q: Population mean is 25, sigma = 10, and n = 64. A sample has M = 27.5. What is its z score?
With MS within = 15 and df within = 36, SS for delay is 250 with df = 1. What is F for delay?
items.why: MS delay = 250/1 = 250 and F = 250/15 = 16.67. The critical F(1, 36) at .05 is 4.11.

items.q: The regression line always passes through
o: The point (mean of X, mean of Y)
items.why: This follows from how the intercept is computed.

items.q: An odds ratio of 4 means the odds of the outcome in the first group are
o: Four times the odds in the second group
items.why: Odds and probability are different. Odds of 4 correspond to a probability of .80.

items.q: In the equation Y-hat = bX + a, b is
o: The slope, the predicted change in Y for each one unit increase in X
items.why: The slope is computed as SP divided by SS of X.

items.q: Anna scored 82 on a test with mean 70 and SD 8. Ben scored 88 on a test with mean 78 and SD 5. Who did better relative to their class?
o: Ben, because his z = 2.00 exceeds Anna's z = 1.50

items.q: A chi-square test is used when the data are
items.why: It compares observed frequencies with expected frequencies.

items.q: The 95 percent CI for the population mean is 55 plus or minus 2.262(2.53). What are the limits?
items.why: 2.262 times 2.53 is 5.72. The CI runs from 49.28 to 60.72 and includes 50, matching the nonsignificant test.

items.q: A study records each participant's diagnosis (depression, anxiety, none). Which graph and summary fit this variable?
o: A bar graph and the mode
A line graph and the median
items.why: Nominal categories are summarized with counts or proportions and the mode. A mean of diagnoses has no meaning.

items.q: For the same study, Cohen's d is the mean difference divided by sigma. What is d?
items.why: d = (79 minus 75)/12 = .33, a small to medium effect. The z of 2.00 mixes effect size with sample size.

items.q: Ice cream sales and drownings are positively correlated across months. What best explains this?
o: A third variable, warm weather, likely drives both
The correlation must be a calculation error
items.why: Season is a classic confounding variable. A correlation alone cannot separate these explanations.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for a goodness-of-fit test with C categories are
items.why: df for a test of independence is (rows minus 1) times (columns minus 1).

items.q: Scores are 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. A student says the SD is 8 because the mean is 8. The error is
o: Confusing the mean with the SD. Variability must come from deviations from the mean
items.why: The mean is 8, and the SD is about 3.16 (SS = 40, sample variance = 10). The SD measures spread, not center.

items.q: Twelve students are tested before and after a workshop. The mean change is +3.0, and the SD of the difference scores is 4.2. What is the estimated standard error?
items.why: sMD = 4.2 divided by the square root of 12 = 1.21.

items.q: What is the estimated standard error of the difference?
items.why: The square root of (30.5/8 + 30.5/8) = the square root of 7.625 = 2.76.

o: A nominal variable with three levels and a numeric variable
items.why: It is Pearson r computed on two variables coded 0 and 1.
